cards.title: Set Up an Automatic Sponsored Products Campaign Inside Out (Split by Targeting Group)
cards.summary: Launch one auto campaign and split close match, loose match, substitutes and compliments into separate ad groups so each match type gets its own bid and its own performance data.
cards.use_when: You are launching Amazon PPC for a new or existing ASIN and want a beginner-safe automatic campaign you can later read and optimize.
steps: In Seller Central open the menu, go to Advertising > Campaign Manager and choose Sponsored Products (source calls this the easiest, most beginner-friendly ad type; Sponsored Brands needs three SKUs and Sponsored Display is covered separately — verify current interface).
Create a campaign, add the product you want to advertise, and select Automatic targeting.
Instead of clicking the single 'set default bid' option, choose to set bids by targeting group so the four automatic groups can be priced separately.

Create one ad group per targeting group rather than running them all together: name the first 'close match' and turn off loose match, substitutes and compliments. Then repeat creating further ad groups named 'loose match', 'substitutes' and 'compliments', each with only its own group enabled.

Use Amazon's suggested bids as a starting point. In the source's example the suggestions were close match $0.92, loose match $0.72, substitutes $0.13, compliments $0.71 — treat these as example values for a sample product, not benchmarks; read your own suggested bids.

Choose a bidding strategy. The source says fixed bids cap you at your max bid and suit tighter cash, while dynamic bids up-and-down can raise your bid up to +100% when Amazon expects a sale and lower it otherwise; dynamic down-only is a middle option. Source used dynamic up-and-down here.

Set the campaign name and start date, and set daily budget to an amount you are willing to lose while the campaign learns — source suggests starting around the recommended daily budget (e.g. $14 in the example) or as low as $5.
Launch the campaign, then return to Campaign Manager to confirm the campaign appears with its ad groups nested underneath.
caveats: Bid suggestion values and available targeting-group options change over time and by product; verify in the current UI before applying.
The source explicitly calls this the very beginner version and defers negative keyword/product targeting and placement bid adjustments to later lessons.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: What Each Amazon Automatic Targeting Group Actually Matches
cards.summary: Understand close match, loose match, substitutes and compliments so you can decide which automatic groups deserve budget and which to switch off.
cards.use_when: You are deciding which automatic targeting groups to enable or how much to bid on each when launching or cleaning up an Amazon auto campaign.
steps: Close match: Amazon shows your ad to shoppers using search terms closely related to your product. Example from the source: for a 400-count cotton sheets product, close match triggers on searches like 'cotton sheets' and '400 count sheets'. This is the group the source says deserves the most spend.

Loose match: shows your ad on search terms loosely related to your product. Same example, loose match could trigger on 'bed sheets' but also 'bath sheets' or 'bath towels' — the source argues this is often irrelevant and not worth heavy budget.
Substitutes: shows your ad on detail pages of products that compete with or substitute for yours (example: your cotton sheets ad on 300-count cotton sheets and queen 400-count sheet listings).
Compliments: shows your ad on detail pages of products that pair with yours (example: queen comforter and feather pillows).

Use the logic rather than the numbers: bid highest on close match, keep substitutes running at the suggested bid as a starting point, and be skeptical of spending heavily on loose match because the intent gap is wide.
After running, judge each group by whether its traffic converts for your product rather than assuming all four are worth keeping.
caveats: The example and bid figures come from one product and one point in time; match definitions are Amazon's and can change, so verify in the current campaign UI.
This is the source's opinion on which group deserves the most money, not a universal rule.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Build Keyword Lists With Magnet: Filtering Rules for Low-Competition Terms
cards.summary: Use the Magnet keyword tool to harvest hundreds of buyer search terms, then filter out head terms and irrelevant queries to build a targetable keyword list.
cards.use_when: You are building the keyword list for a manual Amazon Sponsored Products campaign or deciding which search terms your listing title and bullets should cover.
steps: Seed Magnet with the phrase you believe buyers use (source example: 'carnivore electrolytes'). The tool reports monthly search volume for the seed and generates hundreds or thousands of related terms.
Save results into a named folder (e.g. the product name) so the list carries over to campaign setup.
Sort by the Magnet IQ score to surface the more relevant terms first.

Apply filters to remove terms that are too hard to win: source excluded phrases with more than 5,000 monthly searches and set a minimum word count of 2 so single generic words like 'electrolytes' are dropped as too competitive.

Filter for demand and winnability rather than volume alone: source set competing products max 100 to find low-hanging fruit, and set keyword sales minimum 2 to require at least minimal sales actually flowing through the term.
Hand-pick the survivors for relevance to your exact product before exporting; the source reviewed the filtered list and kept only terms a buyer of that product would plausibly type.
caveats: Thresholds (5,000 searches, 100 competitors, 2 sales, minimum 2 words) are the presenter's heuristics for one product, not validated benchmarks.
Search volume and sales estimates are tool estimates, not Amazon's actual figures.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Manual Keyword Targeting: Broad, Phrase and Exact Match Explained With Ads Implications
cards.summary: Set up a manual keyword campaign and choose broad, phrase or exact match knowing exactly what searches each will trigger and when negative keywords become mandatory.
cards.use_when: You are creating a manual Sponsored Products keyword campaign or diagnosing why a keyword campaign is burning spend on irrelevant search terms.
steps: In Campaign Manager create a new Sponsored Products campaign, name the ad group 'manual keyword targeting', add your product, then choose Manual targeting > Keyword targeting.
Understand the match types before bidding — using the source's example term 'electrolyte powder':
Broad match bids on any search containing 'electrolyte' and 'powder' with other words anywhere in the query, e.g. 'watermelon electrolyte drink powder'.

Phrase match requires the words to stay together with nothing inserted between them, so 'watermelon electrolyte powder' and 'watermelon electrolyte powder drink mix' trigger it but 'watermelon electrolyte drink powder' does not.
Exact match shows only for the query 'electrolyte powder' and nothing more or less; the source calls exact the most powerful match type.

Note the source's observation that exact match was cheaper than phrase or broad for its example product, the reverse of what is usually true — check the suggested bids on your own terms rather than assuming.

Add Amazon's suggested keywords if relevant, or use 'enter list' to paste your filtered keyword list at once; keywords with no suggested bid were assigned $0.92 in the source's example and flagged for later review since no suggestion likely means low search interest.
The source recommends running all three match types but insists that broad and phrase require negative keywords to control waste.
caveats: Match-type behaviour is defined by Amazon and the interface changes; verify current definitions and bid suggestions.
Exact match being cheaper than broad/phrase was an observation on one product, not a rule.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Split Keyword Campaigns Into Themed Ad Groups to See What Makes Money
cards.summary: Organise manual keyword campaigns into topic-based ad groups so you can attribute profit to themes rather than reading one blended number.
cards.use_when: You are structuring manual Amazon PPC campaigns for a product with several distinct buyer intents or sub-audiences.
steps: Group keywords by the buyer intent they represent, not by alphabetical or volume order. Source example: one ad group for the carnivore diet containing all carnivore-related terms, a separate group for flavorless electrolytes (flavorless electrolytes, flavorless electrolyte powder, no flavor electrolyte powder), and a third for meat-based diet because that intent differs from carnivore.
The source notes you can technically run everything in a single ad group to start, but recommends multiple themed ad groups for control.
The practical benefit stated is attribution: separate ad groups let you see which topic actually creates profit so you can shift budget toward it and cut or rework the losers.
Apply the same logic to automatic campaigns by keeping match types in separate ad groups, and to product targeting by keeping competitors in separate ad groups.
Set each campaign's daily budget independently so one theme cannot consume the budget of another.
caveats: More ad groups means more management overhead; the source presents the single ad group as a simpler starting option.
The examples describe one seller's product; group boundaries should follow your own product's intents.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Product Targeting Ads: Run on Competitor Detail Pages (and Group by Competitor to Read Profitability)
cards.summary: Create manual product-targeting Sponsored Products campaigns that place your ad on chosen competitor listings, and split ad groups by brand so you learn which competitor placements pay.
cards.use_when: You want to intercept demand on competitor PDPs or refine a broad category-targeting campaign.
steps: In Campaign Manager create a new Sponsored Products campaign, name the ad group 'product targeting', select the product to advertise, and choose Manual targeting > Product targeting.

Choose between targeting the whole category (e.g. the sports nutrition/endurance/energy powders category) or individual products. The source says category-wide targeting is probably not advisable, though it can be refined.

For individual products, review the suggested product list and deliberately choose the listings most similar to yours — the source says to take time deciding where you want your product to appear rather than adding everything.
Expect these bids to be expensive in some niches; the source notes they were high for its example product.

Group by competitor brand: rather than one ad group with everything, create an ad group containing all products from one brand, and separate ad groups for other brands (source examples: one for Element, one for Liquid IV).
Use the split to compare results — the source's stated goal is to see that advertising on one brand's listings makes money while another brand's placements do not, then act on that.
Optionally use negative product targeting, especially when targeting an entire category, to exclude specific products you don't want to appear beside.
Set daily budget and launch.
caveats: On-page placement beside a competitor does not guarantee conversion; the source frames this as a powerful ad type, not a guaranteed winner.
Bid levels vary by category and time; verify current interface options and suggested bids.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Negative Keywords in Amazon PPC: Exclude Mismatched Formats Before You Spend
cards.summary: Add negative keywords to every campaign so ads don't show for search intent your product cannot satisfy — starting with format and variant mismatches.
cards.use_when: You are launching or optimising any Amazon Sponsored Products campaign and want to reduce wasted clicks on non-buyers.
steps: For each campaign (automatic, manual keyword, product targeting) add negative keywords that tell Amazon not to show your ad when those phrases are searched.

Start by reasoning through your own product: list everything a shopper might search that is related but incompatible. Source example: the electrolytes product ships in a tub, not individual packets, so 'packets' was added as a negative keyword.
Reinforce with data: open Helium 10's Magnet tool, scan the generated search-term list for phrases that would attract the wrong buyer, and add those as negatives.
Apply negatives especially to broad and phrase match campaigns, which the source says require negatives as a condition of running them.
Revisit negatives as you review search-term reports, since new mismatched queries appear over time.
caveats: The source treats negatives as essential for broad/phrase but defers a full negative-targeting lesson; expect a more complete method elsewhere.
Over-blocking can cut legitimate traffic, so review what you exclude rather than blocking loosely related terms blindly.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Target Amazon Keywords by Reverse-Engineering Competitor ASINs (Cerebro / Reverse ASIN)
cards.summary: Pull a competitor's ASIN into a reverse-ASIN tool to see the exact search terms that lead shoppers to find and buy that listing, then build your own target list.
cards.use_when: You are choosing keywords for a new listing, validating product demand, or benchmarking your keyword coverage against a competitor's.
steps: Find the ASIN on the Amazon product page — the source reminds that every Amazon product has an Amazon Standard Identification Number.
Paste the ASIN into Helium 10's Cerebro reverse-ASIN tool.
Read the resulting list of keywords shoppers used to find and purchase that product. Source example: cocktail card searches surfaced terms like 'recipe card deck' and 'recipe cards'.
Use that output in place of guessing: the source says reverse-ASIN is how it actually does product research and claims most sellers are not using it.
Adapt the same method to your own listing by checking which competitor terms you do and don't index for, then adding missing terms to your campaign and listing copy.
Combine with Magnet keyword results so you cover both competitor-proven terms and terms the competitor may not target.
caveats: The source says reverse-ASIN is how it identifies product opportunities — that is a claim based on personal experience, not a guarantee of finding a viable product.
Tool data is estimated from Amazon's data and can be incomplete for low-volume ASINs.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Validate Demand Before You Buy Inventory: Sales Estimator, BSR and Fee Calculator
cards.summary: Estimate a product's monthly revenue and profit before committing inventory by converting BSR with a sales estimator and running the numbers through a fee calculator.
cards.use_when: You are evaluating a product opportunity and need to check whether units sold, price and Amazon's cut leave real profit.
steps: On the product page scroll down and copy the Best Sellers Rank number.
Paste it into the free Jungle Scout sales estimator tool, choose your marketplace and the product's category, and read the estimated units per month.

Multiply estimated units by the product's price to approximate monthly revenue. Source example: this method produced a $60,000/month revenue estimate for one product and a $40,000/month estimate for another.
Do not stop at revenue. Run the same product through an Amazon FBA fee calculator to see actual profit after costs.
Account for at least the referral fee — the source gives an example of a $27.99 product paying a $4.20 referral fee per unit — plus the FBA pick-and-pack fee per unit and other costs.
Alternatively use Helium 10's free extension on the product page to see estimated monthly sales without manual BSR work.
caveats: The source stresses that revenue is not profit; a high-revenue product can be unprofitable after fees.
Estimates are approximations derived from BSR, not actual seller data; treat as directional only.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Find Product Opportunities by Filtering Revenue, Review Count and Category (Blackbox)
cards.summary: Use a product database tool with explicit filters for monthly revenue, review ceiling and category to generate a candidate list instead of browsing randomly.
cards.use_when: You are searching for a product to launch and want a shortlist that matches your revenue target and competitiveness tolerance.
steps: Open a product research database tool (source used Helium 10's Blackbox).
Set a minimum monthly revenue target — source example: at least $10,000 per month.
Set a competition ceiling. The source example used under 400 reviews to find less-contested listings.
Restrict to a category you are willing to operate in; the source used baby as an example of a hot category.
Run the search and work through the returned products, screening for relevance and whether you can realistically source and differentiate.
Supplement with trend tools (source mentions Trendster) to check whether demand in the niche is rising or fading.
caveats: Low reviews can mean the niche is unproven as easily as it can mean it is winnable; the source does not resolve this ambiguity.
Database figures are estimates and category dynamics change; re-run filters periodically.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Pre-Launch Validation With Crowdfunding and Pre-Sales
cards.summary: Reduce the risk of ordering inventory for an unproven product by selling it before manufacturing it, using crowdfunding or similar pre-sale validation.
cards.use_when: You are about to place a first production order for a new product and want evidence people will buy before you commit capital.
steps: Identify the product concept you intend to sell on Amazon.
Run a Kickstarter or Indiegogo campaign for it before buying bulk inventory, so real buyers must commit money.

Use the result as demand evidence: the source raised about $15,000 on its first product this way, and a partner raised over $100,000 with cocktail cards before selling on Amazon, which the source says let them know the products would do well.
Apply the same principle more cheaply if crowdfunding is impractical by creating a pre-order or waitlist offer and measuring real sign-ups.
Only scale into Amazon FBA inventory once pre-sales demonstrate paying demand; treat the raised amounts as case examples, not expected outcomes.
caveats: Crowdfunding campaigns require their own marketing effort and a compelling concept; success is not automatic.
The dollar figures cited are single case results from the source's own products and should not be read as typical.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: FBA vs FBM: Prime Eligibility as a Conversion Lever
cards.summary: Choose Fulfilled by Amazon for the products you want to sell most, because Prime eligibility and Amazon's logistics drive more purchases than the fee savings from self-fulfilling.
cards.use_when: You are deciding how to fulfil a product or considering switching an FBM listing to FBA to lift sales.
steps: Compare the true cost, not just the fee: FBA adds pick-and-pack fees per unit, but FBM requires you to absorb shipping and handling costs yourself, which the source says often narrows the gap.

Weigh the demand side: the source states shoppers strongly prefer Prime-eligible listings and claims sales can be four to five times higher than FBM for the same product — treat that as the presenter's claim from their own experience, not a benchmark.
Test it on your own catalogue: the source's first brand (dance clothing) was entirely FBM; when best-selling items were converted to FBA, sales for those items 'skyrocketed'.
Prioritise converting your best sellers first if you cannot convert everything at once.
caveats: The multiplier claim is the presenter's personal observation and is not independently verified.
FBA fees, dimensions and eligibility rules change; verify current fee schedules before modelling.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Invest in Branding and Packaging Quality Instead of $5 Designs
cards.summary: Cheap logos and packaging suppress conversion on Amazon because shoppers judge the product's credibility from the visual assets before reading copy.
cards.use_when: You are budgeting for product design, logo, packaging or listing imagery before launch or relaunch.
steps: Do not source your logo, branding or packaging from the lowest-price freelance tier. The source describes beginners paying around $5 for these assets and the result looking 'absolutely terrible' with nobody buying.
Treat design spend as conversion infrastructure rather than an avoidable cost — the source frames the cheap option as false economy that costs more in lost sales than it saves.
Apply the same standard to packaging, since it is part of the perceived product quality in Amazon imagery and on arrival.
Judge the spend against expected units sold, not against the cheapest available quote.
caveats: This is the presenter's opinion based on observing student outcomes; it does not set a spending threshold or guarantee returns.
Premium design does not compensate for a product nobody wants — pair with demand validation.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Launch Velocity: Why Early Sales Volume Shapes Amazon Search Placement
cards.summary: Aim to generate concentrated sales in the launch window because Amazon's ranking rewards early sales with higher search placement, and higher placement compounds into more clicks.
cards.use_when: You are planning a product launch window or deciding how much PPC and promotion budget to front-load on a new ASIN.
steps: Accept the ordering logic the source describes: products ranking first get the most clicks, then second, third and fourth, and the drop-off is described as exponential rather than linear.
Therefore treat the first days as the priority spend window: drive as many sales as possible from day one so Amazon reads the listing as relevant and pushes it up in results.

Fund this with a deliberate PPC budget plus any pre-launch demand you built (crowdfunding/pre-sales), and accept that short-run PPC profit may be negative — the source explicitly says you probably will not make much money in the short run with Amazon PPC.
Set the daily budget at an amount you are willing to lose during this learning period rather than at a level that throttles the campaign.
Monitor whether ranking improves; if it does not, the launch tactics or the listing are the problem, not just the budget.
caveats: The source's ranking mechanism description is its own explanation of Amazon's algorithm, not documented Amazon policy.
Spending to rank is a loss-leader strategy that can fail if the product or listing does not convert.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Choosing Between Helium 10 and Jungle Scout: A Function-by-Function Comparison
cards.summary: Pick your Amazon tool stack by which specific capabilities you need — Helium 10 for breadth of research, listing and PPC automation, Jungle Scout for its supplier database.
cards.use_when: You are choosing which paid Amazon research tool to subscribe to, or deciding whether a second tool is justified.
steps: Map your gaps first. Source notes Helium 10 organises tools into product research, keyword research, marketing, listing optimisation, analytics and operations; Jungle Scout groups into product research, suppliers, keywords, marketing, sales analytics and advertising.

If keyword depth matters, note the source's comparison: on the same seed term, Jungle Scout's keyword tool showed roughly 11 filters versus 14 in Helium 10 and returned 49 keyword ideas versus over 1,400, with fewer data columns.

If supplier identification matters, Jungle Scout's supplier database is the standout — the source says you can enter a competitor or similar product and learn who manufactures it, and knows people who keep Helium 10 for research while subscribing to Jungle Scout just for this tool.

Consider pricing structure: the source cites Helium 10 having a free plan plus a 7-day money-back period, and Jungle Scout having no free plan, with a cited offer of three months for $149 (about $49/month) which is more expensive upfront but cheaper monthly and comparable to a Helium 10 tier priced around $79/month.

If PPC automation matters, note Helium 10's Adtomic has no Jungle Scout equivalent (it tiers this to platinum and above), and Helium 10's Refund Genie recovers money Amazon owes you while Jungle Scout has no equivalent.

Compare user experience: source flags Helium 10 as harder for beginners to navigate due to many similarly named tools and a weak mobile experience; Jungle Scout as easier but less capable in data depth and listing-launch support.
Both tools were described as having a 7-day money-back period, so the source suggests trialling one, then the other, and choosing.
caveats: Pricing, plan tiers and feature availability change frequently — verify current plans and any trial or guarantee terms before subscribing.
The stated winner (Helium 10) is the presenter's opinion, and the presenter states an affiliate relationship with both tools.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Using a Listing Analyser and Index Checker to Diagnose Conversion and Rank Gaps
cards.summary: Score your listing against competitors and check which keywords you actually index for, so you can fix the specific weakness instead of rewriting blindly.
cards.use_when: An Amazon listing is getting impressions but weak conversion, or you want to confirm you rank for the keywords you are bidding on.
steps: Run your own product through a listing analyser and read the listing quality score. Source example: a listing scored 7.5, which the source read as leaving room for improvement.

Run the same analysis on competitors to see what they do differently, and use the analyser's recent sales figures (the example reported last-7-days sales) plus historical data as context for how the listing performs.
Use an index checker to confirm whether you actually show up in Amazon search for each keyword you care about, rather than assuming that adding a term to the backend means you rank for it.
Use keyword processing tools (source mentions Frankenstein) to organise and de-duplicate the keyword set before putting terms into title, bullets and backend fields.
Cross-reference with a keyword rank tracker that records position over time so you can confirm whether changes moved you.
Fix the weakest measured area first — copy, imagery or indexing — and re-measure rather than making wholesale changes and losing attribution.
caveats: Quality scores and analysis outputs are tool-generated heuristics; a 7.5 is the source's illustration, not a defined pass/fail threshold.
Some listed tools are tier-gated and the available feature set changes; verify in your current plan.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Recover Amazon's Own Errors and Protect Inventory With Operations Tools
cards.summary: Run scheduled checks that claw back money Amazon owes you and guard against listing hijackers and stockouts, since both quietly destroy Amazon margin.
cards.use_when: You are operating an existing Amazon listing and want to reduce leakage in fees, reimbursements and inventory continuity.
steps: Use a refund/reimbursement tool (source: Helium 10's Refund Genie) to systematically identify money Amazon owes you. The source states plainly that Amazon does not always send what it owes and makes mistakes that cost sellers money.

Use inventory alerts and monitoring so you do not run out of stock. The source warns that running out of inventory risks Amazon treating you as an unreliable or unprofessional seller, which can be far more damaging than the lost sales.
Use alerting that flags hijackers on your listing so unauthorised sellers can be removed before they damage the listing's performance.

Automate post-purchase follow-up emails to prompt reviews — the source lists an automated follow-up tool as part of the standard operations stack; keep within Amazon's messaging rules as they currently stand.
Run these checks on a recurring schedule rather than once, since reimbursements, stock levels and hijack activity all change over time.
caveats: The source's statements about Amazon blacklisting sellers for stockouts are its own characterisation, not a documented policy; verify current Amazon policy and messaging rules.
Automated follow-up and review requests must comply with Amazon's current Terms of Service and messaging rules.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Commit Budget to Tools Early Rather Than Trialling Everything Manually
cards.summary: The source argues that refusing to spend on tooling early is itself the expensive choice, because manual guesswork leads to larger downstream mistakes.
cards.use_when: You are deciding whether to pay for Amazon research, listing or PPC tooling on a tight starting budget.
steps: Recognise the source's position: as a beginner it avoided spending on the belief that spending money equals losing money, and now considers that the wrong calculation.

Use the source's analogy to size the decision: you can build a doghouse with a rock instead of a hammer, but building a mansion justifies buying the tool — invest in proportion to the size of the business you intend to build.

Test cheaply first: several of the recommended tools have free tiers or free versions, and the source says a student found a $100,000/month product using Helium 10's free plan. Helium 10 was also described as having a 7-day money-back period, and Jungle Scout a 7-day guarantee.
If you do pay, start on monthly rather than annual billing if you are only doing a short product-research sprint, and switch to annual only once you know you will keep the tool.

Note the source's stated losses from under-investing and other mistakes: thousands on manufacturing issues, tens of thousands on expiring excess inventory, and over $100,000 attributed to the other mistakes discussed — treat these as the presenter's own figures, not typical outcomes.
Weigh tool cost against the cost of the mistake it prevents (buying wrong inventory, unprofitable PPC, penalties).
caveats: The dollar figures are the presenter's personal losses and are not benchmarks.
The presenter has affiliate relationships with the tools recommended, which is a conflict to account for.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Amazon Referral Fees and Unit Economics: Start With the 15% Cut
cards.summary: Before locking a price, model the referral fee as a percentage of sale price plus per-unit fulfilment cost so a healthy-looking price still leaves profit.
cards.use_when: You are setting or revising a product price, or checking whether a sourced product can be profitable at the price the market supports.
steps: Count the three major FBA cost blocks the source identifies: the Amazon referral fee, the FBA pick-and-pack (fulfilment) fee, and other costs.

Understand the referral fee as a flat percentage charged for selling on Amazon, which the source says depends on the product's price. Source example: a product priced at $27.99 pays a referral fee of $4.20 per unit sold, which is roughly 15% — the source separately states sellers pay 15% for the Amazon selling fee.
Apply the fee per unit, not per order or per month, when calculating contribution margin.
Add the pick-and-pack fee per unit on top of the referral fee, since the referral fee alone does not include fulfilment.
Enter price and dimensions into an Amazon FBA fee calculator to get the net profit figure rather than estimating by hand.
Re-check fees after any price change or product/packaging change, since the referral fee scales with price while fulfilment fees depend on size and weight.
caveats: The 15% figure and the $27.99 / $4.20 example are illustrative; referral fee percentages vary by category and Amazon's fee schedules change, so verify current rates.
Some product categories have minimum referral fees that matter more on low-priced items.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Cheap Ways to Get Amazon Data Without Paying: Free Tools and Scorecards
cards.summary: Run initial product screening with free tools and structured criteria before paying for any subscription, so budget goes only where it changes a decision.
cards.use_when: You are starting Amazon product research with no budget and need a practical workflow that still produces a real decision.
steps: Use the Amazon FBA fee calculator to check profit on candidate products — the source lists this as a free tool.
Use the free Jungle Scout sales estimator for unit estimates by pasting the BSR; note that the free version caps how many times you can use it per day, and the paid version removes that cap.
Use the free Helium 10 extension on any product page to see estimated monthly sales without manually looking up BSR.
Use Helium 10's free plan for keyword and product research with some restrictions — the source says it personally knows a student who found a $100,000/month product using the free plan.

Build a scorecard before spending: for each candidate record estimated units, price, estimated revenue, fee-adjusted profit, review count and category, then compare candidates against each other rather than one at a time.
Only upgrade to a paid tool when a specific research task is blocked, not pre-emptively.
caveats: Free tier caps and available features change; verify what your current free plan includes.
Free estimates are approximations and should not be the sole basis for a large inventory commitment.
cards.source_name: FREE Amazon FBA Course _ 12 Hour FULL Step by Step Tutorial 2025.docx

cards.title: Avoid the Big Beginner Amazon Mistakes: Wrong Product, FBM by Default, Cheap Assets
cards.summary: Three recurring beginner errors — unvalidated product choice, defaulting to merchant fulfilment, and underinvesting in branding — account for most of the money the source sees lost.
cards.use_when: You are in the early planning stage of an Amazon launch and want to sequence your decisions to avoid expensive rework.
steps: Do not buy inventory on thin research. The source describes beginners doing a little research, ordering 1,000 units, and discovering nobody wants the product. Validate demand first with keyword search volume data and, preferably, pre-sales or crowdfunding before placing a bulk order.

Do not default to FBM just because fees look lower. The source argues Prime eligibility drives materially more purchases and gives the example of its own dance-clothing brand where converting best sellers from FBM to FBA caused sales to 'skyrocket'.
Do not buy $5 logos, branding and packaging from budget freelancers; the source says the result looks terrible and nobody buys, framing it as false economy.
Sequence accordingly: prove demand, then design the brand assets, then fulfil via FBA for the products you most want to sell.

Treat every figure in the source's own loss history — thousands on manufacturing, tens of thousands on expiring inventory, over $100,000 on other mistakes — as the presenter's experience, useful as a warning about cost categories rather than a prediction for your business.
caveats: The sales multiplier from FBA and the loss figures are personal observations, not measured benchmarks.
The source says these mistakes are avoidable based on observing over a thousand students, which is a claim of pattern, not proof of causation.

cards.title: Launch Product Demand Research From a Theme Tool and a Seed Phrase
cards.summary: Use a keyword tool's related-term output as a product-idea generator, not just as a campaign keyword list, because it reveals adjacent buyer needs you could sell into.
cards.use_when: You have a product category or audience in mind and want to identify a specific product to launch, rather than a keyword list for an existing one.
steps: Enter a seed phrase describing what buyers type — the source used 'cocktail cards' and found over a thousand monthly searches, which was how the cocktail cards product was originally identified.

Read the adjacent terms the tool returns as product ideas, not just bid terms. Source example: 'easy cocktail recipe book' at over 200 searches per month, and a much larger unrelated term like 'card shuffler' at over 26,000 searches per month which is a signal about the broader gift/card category rather than a term to bid on.
Sort by search volume to see the shape of the niche, then look for a cluster where volume exists and competition is beatable rather than chasing the single biggest term.
Cross-check any candidate against a reverse-ASIN lookup on the closest existing product to see the full set of terms buyers use to find and buy it.
Use misspelling tools to capture common misspellings in backend keywords as an additional free source of impressions.
caveats: High-volume adjacent terms can be irrelevant to your product; the source treats them as category signal, not automatic targets.
Search volumes are tool estimates and shift seasonally.
